statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail holds at 22% as a confirmed 0.81% retracement and a cash index trading below its own open offset a partial futures recovery toward the record-area high.
recommendation: Tail remains inside the watch band at 22%, so the mapped policy state stays WATCH. The retracement observed an hour ago has held: NQ has recovered to 31,114.75 but has not reclaimed the 31,282.50 session high, and cash NDX at 30,836.57 trades below its own 30,869.14 opening print, meaning the cash session has given back its entire opening gain. That is direct evidence that mean reversion is functioning at a record-area level, and it is why no slot in this publication reaches the block band. Tail is also not reduced further, because the 10-year has set a 5.26% session high against a rallying index, an unresolved cross-asset conflict, and because the Friday power hour, the cash close and a weekend closure still lie ahead with the Iran conflict unresolved and a four-month G7 barrel release beginning. The narrow danger window covers 19:00Z to 21:00Z, the power hour through the weekly futures settlement, rather than the whole session.
headline: NQ holds 31,114.75 with a confirmed 0.81% retracement behind it while cash NDX trades below its 30,869.14 open and the 10-year sets a 5.26% session high
body: NQ December futures trade 31,114.75 (+354.25, +1.15%) on a quote timed 16:20:05Z, inside a 30,760.25-31,282.50 session range from a 30,771.25 open on about 424k contracts, with a 31,114.75/31,115.25 bid/ask. The structural point of this hour is that the retracement flagged at 15:37Z has held rather than been erased. NQ has recovered roughly 85 points from the 31,029.75 pullback low but remains 167.75 points, 0.54%, below the session high, and it has not printed a new high. The cash index is weaker still: NDX is 30,836.57 (+335.01, +1.10%) at 16:25:39Z against a 30,869.14 open and a 31,017.53 session high, so the cash session itself is marginally negative from its opening print and sits 0.58% off its high. The Nasdaq Composite set an all-time high earlier in the session and has since retreated from it. Taken together these are two-way observations, not persistent directional efficiency, and they are why Tail stays in the watch band instead of returning to the block band it occupied at 14:00Z. The driver of the move is verified: the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported September nonfarm payrolls of +29,000 against a 90,000 consensus, unemployment at 4.2% and average hourly earnings up 0.1% on the month and 3.0% on the year. That miss cut October rate-hike odds from about 64% a week ago to roughly 16%, which is the mechanism behind a 1%-plus index advance. Single-name leadership is confirmed but off its extremes: NVDA 236.38 (+2.39%) is below the 237.87 intraday record it set earlier, SMH 633.63 (+2.56%) is 2.62 points under its 636.25 high, and Tesla trades sharply higher after reporting 486,532 third-quarter deliveries against a 461,974 company-compiled consensus. The cross-asset picture conflicts with the equity bid rather than confirming it. The 10-year yield is 5.26%, up 0.03 and at the top of a 5.16-5.27 session range, so the long end has fully reversed its post-payrolls rally while equities held their gain; the 2-year is near 4.83-4.84%. VIX is 15.55, down 5.13%, with a 15.42 session low, an absolute level inconsistent with violent repricing. Energy is the dominant macro channel and it is unusually volatile: WTI is near $90.62, down about 2.4% inside an $88.11-$93.51 range, after the G7 agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel reserves over four months with a substantial diesel tranche inside twenty days; Brent remains above $100 and diesel near $6.37 a gallon following the February escalation with Iran. That combination, a soft labour print, an unresolved inflation channel and a long end at session highs, supports high Stress at 79% while leaving Tail at 22%. Confidence is 89%: current verified levels are held for NQ, NDX, VIX, the 2-year and 10-year, WTI, Brent, SMH and NVDA, together with the primary payrolls release, the seven-day calendar and the verified FOMC minutes date. The shared Finviz context file was read and rejected for material use: its most recent collection is dated 29 September with a partial status and unavailable futures and calendar sections, far outside the 90-minute freshness limit, so this assessment rests entirely on independent current research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours are available, covering the 16:00Z hour on 1 October through the 15:00Z hour today. Tail ran from 20% to 27% across the window. It opened at 20% and held that watch floor for fifteen consecutive hours, through the U.S. afternoon on 1 October and the whole Asian session, then stepped to 21% at 07:00Z, 23% at 08:00Z and 22% at 09:00Z as the European-morning advance gained directional efficiency. It returned to 20% for the 10:00Z and 11:00Z hours, then climbed through the payrolls release to 24% at 12:00Z, 25% at 13:00Z and a window peak of 27% at 14:00Z, the only two hours published in the block band, when NQ was holding within 0.10% of its session extreme with no meaningful pullback. The 15:00Z hour mapped back to 22% once a 0.81% retracement was actually observed. Stress stayed in the high band throughout, between 74% and 79%, and Confidence held 88-89%. Dominant mode was mixed for most of the window, with trend-up recorded only for the 08:00Z and 09:00Z European-morning hours and the 12:00Z to 14:00Z post-payrolls stretch.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail at 22% for the current 16:00Z hour and the 17:00Z hour, then eases to 21% at 18:00Z on assumed range containment between the 30,760.25 low and the 31,282.50 high. No slot is published in the block band, because the amplifier stack that supported it at 14:00Z has been invalidated by an observed retracement that held, by a cash index trading under its own opening print, and by an absolute VIX near 15.55. A three-point uplift to 24% covers 19:00Z and 20:00Z, the Friday power hour and the cash close, where weekly-close and market-on-close flow meets a record-area level against a long end that has already reversed once today; that pairing is the published danger window, extended to 21:00Z to include the weekly futures settlement. The escalation condition on those hours is a loss of the 31,029.75 pullback low together with a 10-year break above the 5.27% session high; the invalidation is an orderly close that keeps NQ inside today's range. CME equity index futures settle for the week at 21:00Z and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, so the final eighteen slots sit entirely inside a market closure and carry a flat 20% watch floor rather than a projected curve. A closed market offers no price path to deny, while mapping an unresolved record-area weekly close into the lowest band would misrepresent it as benign. Stress steps from 79% to 78% and then to 77% from 07:00Z on the assumption that no fresh weekend escalation emerges, and Confidence decays from 89% to 72% across the closed stretch because ageing evidence degrades certainty about the state rather than the state itself. The first live catalyst is Monday's 14:00Z ISM Services PMI; Wednesday's 18:00Z FOMC minutes are the most credible delayed-second-leg mechanism for the long end; September CPI is verified for 14 October and therefore sits outside this window.
